summary: MISO answers the comments and protests on its large-load reliability proposal, defends its definitions, transition provisions and Tariff/BPM split, and asks FERC to accept the proposal unchanged.
ask: Accept the answer and accept the IRR Proposal without modification or condition, effective December 4, 2026.

points.point: MISO says the pleadings broadly support the proposal and only one protest asks for rejection with refiling by end of 2027.
points.quote: only one protest requests the revisions to be rejected and MISO directed to file revised requirements by the end of 2027.

points.point: MISO says the comments offer alternatives but do not show the proposal fails section 205.
points.quote: but do not establish that the framework proposed by MISO fails to satisfy the requirements of Section 205 of the Federal Power Act.

points.point: MISO asks that the proposal be accepted without modification and without expanding the proceeding to other large-load issues.
points.quote: MISO respectfully requests that the IRR Proposal be accepted without modification and grant the requested effective date of December 4, 2026.

points.point: MISO ties the proposal to the E-8 findings on a large load definition and ongoing operational requirements.
points.quote: a definition of large load sufficient to capture loads that present the unique challenges described in the Show Cause Order

points.point: On scope, MISO says the proposal does not create a regime for distribution-connected load not taking MISO Transmission Service.
points.quote: the IRR Proposal does not create a free-standing MISO reliability regime for distribution- connected load that is not taking MISO Transmission Service.

points.point: MISO's conclusion requests acceptance without modification or condition.
points.quote: MISO respectfully requests that the Commission (i) accept this Answer and (ii) accept the IRR Proposal without modification or condition.

throughLine.text: MISO's reply to protests of its first filing after the E-8 order, defending it as a response to the order's findings on large load definition and ongoing operational requirements.
